title: Reading heatmap + sprint sketch: inference patterns and paper takeaways
content:
Quick intent: synthesize a small “heatmap” of inference research (papers + talks I saw at MLSys/MLSys-satellite mini-summits) and map each region to concrete micro-experiments we can run on Redwood infra. Keep this informal — thinking-out-loud, sketches, and explicit next steps for a 1-week exploratory sprint.

Top-level thesis / framing
- Problem: there6s a bunch of incremental inference work that each targets slightly different axes (per-token cost, tail latency, memory pressure for KV cache, quality regression with quant/opt). We need a compact view that maps workload shapes -> best candidate optimization(s) + risk profile. That6s the heatmap.
- Goal: produce a 2x2 (or 3x3) heatmap for developer-facing guidance and a short experiment matrix (N=8 cheap experiments) to validate on Redwood-hosted and a Dedicated pool.

Notes from the talks/papers (raw):
1) "Sparse KV-MoE caches for long contexts" (arXiv:2806.01234)
   - Idea: maintain multiple small per-token caches (key shards) and route queries to small specialized MoE caches instead of a global dense KV. Good when contexts are heterogeneous (chat+code + retrieval).
   - Claims: 2-3x latency improvement on tail percentiles with small model overhead; modest quality drop if routing is noisy.
   - Implementation sketch: need fast lookups + routing table; interacts with batch composition — if routing skews, we get uneven GPU utilization.

2) "Quant-aware attention kernels" (arXiv:2805.09876)
   - Low-bit kernels that keep attention softmax in fp16 but store large matrices in 4-bit with per-block scaling. Observed tiny quality loss when combined with layer-wise distillation. Very attractive for cost savings.
   - Risk: operator support across platforms (A100 vs H100 vs AMD) and fallback behavior.

3) "Adaptive batching for tail-Latency SLOs" (poster + code)
   - Dynamic batch shaping at request arrival time: give priority to small-latency requests, opportunistically piggyback small ones into a running batch using additive deadlines.
   - Aligns with Redwood6s routing policies: can be a per-tenant runtime policy.

4) "Eviction heuristics for long-context caches" (workshop notes)
   - Empirical result: LRU is fine for conversational logs, but semantic eviction (topic change detection + TTL per-topic) reduces cache pollution and improves quality while keeping cache size constant.

Heatmap axes proposal (first pass)
- X axis: inference workload skew (uniform vs heavy-tail per-key reuse)
- Y axis: quality sensitivity (high: summarization/medical vs low: code-completion toy app)
- Third dimension (annotated): tail-latency sensitivity (high/medium/low) via color intensity.

Mapping ideas (cells -> candidate optimizations + risk)
- Uniform reuse + low quality sensitivity: 4-bit quant + aggressive batching. Low risk, high cost savings. Micro-exp: quantize Llama-compat model 4-bit w/ block scaling, run on dedi small pool.
- Heavy reuse + high quality sensitivity: KV prefix caching + semantic eviction + conservative quant (8-bit or none). Risk: storage/eviction complexity; experiment: simulate session traces from product logs, replay against cache variants.
- Heavy reuse + low quality sensitivity: KV shards / sparse MoE caches (paper 1) + aggressive eviction heuristics. Risk: routing skew -> throughput drop; experiment: synthetic long-tail traces and measure utilization on batchers.
- Uniform + high quality sensitivity: can6t quantize aggressively; prioritize adaptive batching to keep tail latency tight.

Experiment matrix (cheap-ish first week)
- E1: 4-bit block quant inference on hosted sandbox (small cluster) using two representative models (open-llm A & B). Metrics: tokens/op, sample-quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE for synthetic), percentiles (p50,p95,p99). Linked artifact: PR #42.
- E2: Replay 1-week of anonymized chat traces (synthetic) against LRU vs semantic-eviction policy for a 32k KV cache. Measure: cache hit rate, quality delta on held-out prompts.
- E3: Implement mini sparse-KV routing (Python prototype) and run micro-bench on single GPU to observe lookup overhead and batch-utilization.
- E4: Adaptive batching simulation in the local batcher: inject mixes of small/large requests, emulate deadlines. Measure percentiles and throughput.
- E5: Test quant-aware attention kernels fallback on H100 vs A100 (via dedicated pool). Document any kernel selection mismatches and operator fallbacks.
- E6: Small distillation pass for 2 layers (teacher: full precision, student: 4-bit sim). Measure quality delta on targeted tasks.
- E7: Integrate a lightweight "heatmap" dashboard (not polished) into a notebook: cells show which optimization to try given workload signature.
- E8: Quick cost model: token-cost delta + infra delta per strategy (bucketed) so PM can see $$ impact.

Data & replay notes (practical)
- Need sanitized session traces (only timing + token counts + coarse category: code/chat/doc). PII removal required — talk to legal.
- If traces unavailable, build synthetic mixes: (a) chat-heavy (many small messages), (b) retrieval + long context (large context tokens, repeated prefixes), (c) code-iteration (short but high-quality).

Open questions / risks / decisions
- How aggressive can we be with quant on models customers rely on? Need to mark as experimental and expose "quality-metrics" gate in Console.
- For sparse-KV routing: does Redwood6s routing layer support per-request routing decisions fast enough? If not, we may need an in-GPU tiny routing map staged per-batch.
- Operator portability: some optimizations depend on custom CUDA kernels — need fallback paths to maintain Hosted SLA.

Action items (next 7 days)
- Nikhil: spin up E1 baseline (4-bit quant) on sandbox — target completion 2028-06-18. (linked PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-heatmap-probes/pull/42)
- Maya: source 1-week anonymized trace or synthetic generator by 2028-06-16.
- Samir: prototype sparse-KV routing microbench by 2028-06-21.
- Schedule 30m sync with infra SRE to confirm Dedicated pool kernel selection behavior (SLO implications) — target 2028-06-15.

Things I want to record (notes-to-self)
- Keep heatmap small; product folks will prefer 4-6 actionable cells not an academic taxonomy.
- Emphasize risk gating: label experiments as: exploratory / prod-safe / requires-approval.
- Consider hooking the small dashboard to Console as a "suggested optimization" card (future).

Raw links & refs I want to read more carefully:
- Sparse KV-MoE caches (paper): https://arxiv.org/abs/2806.01234
- Quant-aware attention kernels: https://arxiv.org/abs/2805.09876
- Adaptive batching repo (poster): https://github.com/adaptive-batching/example
- Related internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-heatmap-probes/pull/42

Back-of-envelope expected outcomes (if E1-E4 go well)
- We get a quick internal doc mapping 3 workload archetypes -> 2 recommended optimizations each.
- Cost model suggests a potential 25-45% token-cost reduction on low-quality-sensitivity workloads with quant + batching.
- One small insight: semantic-eviction might be low-hanging fruit for conversational customers (small dev effort, high payoff).

Misc scratch (phrases to use in final doc)
- "workload signature" = (median message length, reuse skew, task-quality-sensitivity)
- "risk gate" = {exploratory | prod-safe | requires-approval}
- "heatmap cell" -> short recipe: model, cache policy, quant level, routing policy.
